Subject: Request: full subprocessor inventory + export paths for DPA review

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked solid. As part of our legal review ahead of procurement approval, we need a complete subprocessor inventory and a quick note on any cross‑border export paths tied to the processors listed. Specifically: 

- A CSV list (name, service provided, country of processing, whether they have access to customer content, KMS/HSM involvement)
- Which subprocessors may result in data egress outside the EU/UK/US (we're primarily focused on EU controls for our EEA users)
- Any temporary or fallback processors used for burst/autoscale scenarios (and duration limits)

Can you send the inventory and confirm whether the current DPA (we shared a template last month) covers temporary processors and escrow/onshore fallback? If you can attach the inventory and a point of contact in infra/legal, that would help speed our internal sign‑off.

Appreciate it — aim is to close procurement by next Wednesday.

Best,
Alice Turner
Senior Privacy Counsel
ClearWave Analytics

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list.

Sharing a preliminary inventory (see attachment). Key notes up front:

- Inventory covers production processors only; temporary burst partners are flagged in the last column.
- We call out whether each processor touches customer content (yes/no) and the KMS jurisdiction.
- For EU/EEA data: default routing keeps traffic within EU regions; fallback to non‑EU regions happens only in exceptional capacity events and is limited to 90 minutes per event — we log and audit each occurrence.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Lauren can confirm whether the current DPA language (esp. the subprocessor paragraph and export control clauses) is sufficient or needs a narrow addendum for temporary processors.
2) Jonas can provide the technical export path map (if you need packet/egress-level detail).

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20290630.csv (CSV)

Thanks — we can iterate quickly. If you give a preferred format for the export path detail (diagram vs table), we’ll produce that today.

Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessor inventory + export paths for DPA review

Alice / team — looping in legal counsel for the DPA specifics. A couple quick clarifications from our side that will help speed a sign‑off: 

- The attached DPA_redlines_v3.pdf highlights two proposed edits: one to explicitly list temporary/burst subprocessors as covered by the DPA and a second to add a maximum duration for cross‑border fallbacks.
- We propose adding a single sentence to the subprocessor clause referencing our subprocessor roster (we publish the inventory and update it per the DPA notice period) and a right to notify customers 30 days in advance for non‑emergency additions. Emergency short‑term processors remain covered but we’ll include audit evidence on request.
- On KMS/HSM: our standard is that customer data encryption keys are tenant‑scoped and managed in KMS controlled by Redwood; subprocessors that handle backups/archives do not have key material unless explicitly provisioned for support (we call those out in the inventory under "KMS access").

Action items for ClearWave to confirm: 
- Do you require SCCs for each processor, or is a combination of SCCs + vendor attestations acceptable?
- For procurement timeline: is a signed DPA enough to proceed to purchase order, or do you need additional SOC2 artifacts and recent penetration test evidence attached to the DPA?

We can produce a short evidence packet (SOC2 report redacted + penetration test summary + topology diagram) within 48 hours if that helps.

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf (PDF)

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Legal Lead, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@clearwave.com>

Cc: security@clearwave.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 15:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessor inventory + export paths for DPA review

Thanks Soojin / Lauren — this is helpful. A few follow ups before we loop procurement: 

- SCCs: we prefer SCCs for any processor that persists EEA customer content. For processors that only process metadata (no content) an attestation + contractual clause is acceptable. Can you flag those two categories in the CSV?
- Evidence: signed DPA + SOC2 Type II (latest 12 months) will be required to enable our finance team to issue the PO. A penetration test summary is appreciated but not mandatory for initial PO.
- Emergency processors: the 90‑minute fallback policy is acceptable if you provide audit logs for each event and a named contact that will provide a post‑incident evidence package within 72 hours.

If you can: 
1) Update CSV to include an "SCC required" column and a "processor category: content|metadata" value.
2) Share SOC2 redaction + DocuSign link for the DPA (we can run signature once redlines are agreed).

Procurement target remains next Wednesday; if you can get the updated CSV and DocuSign draft to me EOD tomorrow, I’ll push for internal approval.

Onward — will await the updated files.

Best,
Alice Turner
Senior Privacy Counsel
ClearWave Analytics
